text: adversarial finding: Every residue can hold while a player who dies never comes back: the play probe runs in god mode, so the checkpoints and the mod's respawn are never exercised in 06's layered geometry (a cap, the deck, the tower).
adversarial finding: boat-run only proves the boat goes east; 'vehicles fit and can leave' also needs it to back out of the lane's end and return west.
adversarial finding: The command room is only reached through the tower's own ladder shaft, but the objective test teleports into it; the tower climb itself is never played.
adversarial finding: look-dusk-palette measures colour only: an image of mostly sky-coloured emptiness could pass it. The structure (bands top to bottom, where the detail is) must match too.
adversarial finding: The emergent property 'each foundation reads as a distinct fight with cover, height and a flank' has no residue: the caps as first built are flat slabs.

adversarial finding: coop-two can pass while guests can't use the ladders (the ladder code moves characters on the host from their controllers' inputs; a guest's input path differs from the host's keyboard).
adversarial finding: Editor saveability: the level is built only from the editor's own templates plus registered mod entities, which the linter parses; no separate residue needed.
adversarial finding: The hanging-container jump chain is an optional route; the linter proves the jumps are within the rules. Not material.
adversarial finding: 'CS enemies hold every layer' has no residue: all enemies could sit on one layer and every other residue still hold.
adversarial finding: 'CS patrol boats drive the lane by autopilot' is unverified in 06: the boat test only records where the patrols ended.
adversarial finding: Co-op strength for 3 and 4 players rests on the names: nothing checks that 06 has enough [2+] and [3+] enemies to scale.

adversarial finding: Round 3: with respawn, the boat backing out, the tower climb, structure as well as palette, cap cover, guest ladders, layers held, patrols and co-op names covered, nothing material is left that no residue would catch. The remaining risk is in the probes themselves (a harness test that passes for the wrong reason), which FINAL_VERIFY re-examines against the evidence.

ladders-work: the swimmer was put at x 2583, 13 px from the water ladder at 2570 (inside its 55 px catch), yet in 4 s with W held it went 470 px west to x 2114 and never took the ladder (ladder 0 throughout). The same test passed in cycles 9 and 10 from the same spot, and the shaft climb and the road exit in this very run took their ladder (shaftTop ladder 1). What differs is the test before it: the boat test ends driving west with A held, and put() only zeroes the ragdoll atoms' velocities (labkit.still), not the character's own bodies.

The swimmer's drift is the boat's momentum surviving the teleport: the operator's scratch trail probe (outside the store) put a fresh swimmer at the same ladder six times from 5-45 px off, and it took the ladder and reached the top every time. The probe's put() should still every body (ragdoll atoms and the character's box2d_body, gy, lS), and the water climb should keep a trail so a failure explains itself.

ladders-work's downOk passed on a free fall: the player put on the road over the hatch, S held, ended on the cap at feet -330 with ladder 0 — the probe cannot tell riding the ladder from falling through the hatches. The descent needs a strict test: from beside the hatch, walked onto it with S held, the ladder taken over the hole and kept to its foot (no sample off the ladder between road and cap, no fall speed).

The ladder code itself has a low-frame-rate gap the strict descent would expose: W or S take a ladder only within 28 px of its middle, while a hatch is 140 px wide and a slow frame moves a walker ~60-90 px, so a player walking onto a hatch with S held can be carried past the grab window and fall; the fall catch only applies when nothing is held; and a ladder taken at the catch width (70) is let go the next tick by the 28 px stay check; and left/right held with up/down carries a climber off mid-shaft.

enemies-path: every soldier near the bait (5700, -664) moved 0 px in 20 s — hunters and posts alike, and the patrol crews — while three far soldiers moved (one fell off the cliff, two walked toward the dock). The probe's own shot shows the player's HUD as 'CS PATROL BOAT - DRIVER': the player was not at the bait. The probe hooks only the ragdoll's damage (fire, the CS Heavy's flamethrower 780 px away, does not come through it) and never takes the player out of the boat or checks where it waited; a dead player respawns at the dock, in the boat.

frame-cost: perf (player stood at each spot) gives deck 683 ms / 666 draws, tower span 517, start 633, road 333 against a 183 ms baseline: worst 3.73x. The cycle's breakdown at (8400, -700) is not comparable: perf-breakdown teleports the player without taking it out of the boat, so its asIs/allAsleep/noEnemies steps measured the soldiers near the dock, not the deck.

Where the deck's frame goes (operator's scratch runs outside the store, same session baseline 133 ms): as is 383 ms / 532 draws; every soldier asleep 267 / 352; no enemies 217 / 290; no enemies and no set pieces 167 / 267; half resolution changes little (not fill-bound); no shader programs are linked while measuring; the main thread idles 50-65% (the software rasteriser's draw cost, not script). ThinkNow is 6-9 ms and the render call 15-23 ms of script time. Hiding every soldier's parts for the render saves ~55 ms. So the cost is draw calls — ~0.6-0.8 ms each — from the soldiers (drawn wherever they are) and their fire, and the set pieces (~2 ms each: 23 draws, 50 ms). Even the empty deck is 1.63x the baseline.

Next actions: the staged mod (the review batch plus: ladders — S takes a ladder anywhere over its hatch (60 px), a fast fall is caught whatever is held, a taken ladder holds its climber over the whole hatch, left/right ignored while climbing; characters well off camera hidden for the render only; the cliff tunnel's and the bunker's lower corridor's ceilings raised to 175 px headroom; debug hooks to measure by kind), baked; the play probe (put() stills every body; the water climb with a trail and a swim-in variant; the strict descent; the objective's full hold; respawn time and place; only live crewed patrols counted); the pathing probe (out of the boat, healed every frame, the player's place checked). Next cycle: perf.js made as honest (healed every frame, the player's place checked) and an in-loop frame matrix repeating the scratch measurements.

frame-cost is likely not reachable at 1.5x under the software renderer with the level's fights intact: the empty deck alone measured 1.63x in the operator's run. The remaining reductions (render-time culling of off-camera soldiers, cheaper set pieces) will be measured in-loop first; if the busiest spot stays above 1.5x, the threshold is the human's to decide, not the loop's to move.
unknown: Whether the heavy's eastward walk is the AI hunting another known threat or a path around something between it and the bait.

ladders-work: capOk (direct and swim-in) and roadOk pass; the water trail shows the ladder taken at once (ladder 1 from the first sample) and the swim-in taken on arrival. downOk fails only at the foot: took at x 2014 on the road (feet -859, 466 ms), descent 100-110 px per sample, never off the ladder (offAbove 0, fastest 350 px/s), but the end state is feet -284, ladder 1 — 46 px below the cap's top, inside the cap, still held. The last tick can step past the foot (up to 260 px/s x 0.25 s), and a ghosted climber with nothing held drifts down: the mod zeroes its velocity each tick but gravity acts within the physics steps of a slow frame.

respawn-works: gone and back (5.7 s; back at x 13885, feet -330, 125 px from the checkpoint at 13760), but 3 s later the player was at x 14112, feet -118, falling down the basement shaft (hatch at 14100 +-70). The checkpoint is 140 px from 'CS Bunker guard' (post, 13900) and 490 px from the shotgun hunter (14250): a respawn into point-blank fire, and a knock into the shaft. A design flaw, not the probe's: checkpoints should not stand in a post's face.

enemies-path: the player held the bait (no deaths, never in a vehicle) but was knocked to x 5950 (worst 250 px), so the probe failed itself. Hunters answered: the 7250 trooper (now a hunter) closed 639 px; the road trooper walked 571 px to the hatch above the bait (closer 131); the marksman closed 148; the heavy went 1394 px east; one trooper fell into the sea. Only one crossed 150.

The pathing window is short in game time: the engine's ThinkNow is given GSPEED in 30 fps ticks, and an operator measurement outside the store (6 s at level 06 as tester) gave 116.65 ticks in 5.74 s — the game runs at about 0.68x wall time here, less when frames are heavier. 20 game seconds, the residue's reading of '20 s', need ~30 wall seconds. The probe should count game time, and put a knocked player back at the bait (a waiting player holds its ground).

frame-cost: perf with the player stood at each spot: baseline 133 ms; start 333, tower span 617 (801 draws), deck 633 (550), road 400: worst 4.76x. Draw counts moved from cycle 11 (deck 666 -> 550, tower span 664 -> 801): the cost follows the fight at the spot. Hiding off-camera soldiers is in, but the spots are where the soldiers are.
coop-ladder and coop-two still hold with the new ladder code: the guest took the water ladder (ladder 1 from the third sample) and climbed to the top (-400).

Next: the mod — a climber held at a tracked position each tick (moved by the climb, never past the top or the foot, put back where it sank), let go standing at the foot; the bunker checkpoint moved out onto the catwalk (13440: 460 px from the post, outside the door, clear of both hatches); baked. The pathing probe counting 20 s of game time and putting a knocked player back. perf.js made as honest (healed every frame, out of any vehicle, stilled, its place checked before and after each spot). After: an in-loop frame matrix at the deck.

CHANGED_HYPOTHESIS: The regression (3 -> 4 open) is respawn-works, and it is not the respawn code: the respawn put the player back in 5.7 s, standing, 125 px from the checkpoint; the checkpoint itself stands 140 px from a guard post inside the bunker door, next to the basement shaft's open hatch, and the stricter probe (standing 3 s after) exposed that. Changed hypotheses for the three that keep failing: ladders-work fails at the ladder's foot (overshoot and a sinking ghost), not in taking the ladder — the water, swim-in and shaft climbs now pass; enemies-path fails on the probe's clock and a knock, not on the level's paths — hunters answered once the player was really there, in 20 wall seconds that were ~13 game seconds; frame-cost is the soldiers' fight at the spot under the software renderer, to be measured in-loop by a matrix next.
unknown: Whether the heavy's eastward walk is caused by the hatches (a path around) or by its own hunting of another threat.

ladders-work holds: downTrail [2060,-860,0] -> [2008,-837,1] ... [1980,-416,1] -> [1980,-330,0]: taken over the hatch, down at up to 340 px/s, let go at the foot standing (down: feet -330, ladder 0). The water trail and the swim-in trail take the ladder on arrival. The tracked hold fixed the foot.

respawn-works: gone -> back in 5.7 s; the first sample alive was x 13345, feet -330 — 95 px from the checkpoint now on the catwalk (13440) — and 3 s later x 13180, feet -330, standing on the catwalk. The probe's atCheckpoint read the 3-s-later place (a knock along the floor under fire), while the property is where the respawn puts the player. The review's wording was 'back within 8 s and within 150 px of the checkpoint': judged at the first moment back.

enemies-path: with the player held at the bait (20.5 game s over 30.6 wall s; 5 put-backs; no deaths; never in a vehicle), movedCount 2 (the road marksman closed 211, the road trooper 152) and anyMoved 7; the rest went away: a deck trooper 875 px off, the heavy 1475 east, a cap trooper into the sea.

The 140 px shaft hatches cut the AI's floors (operator's scratch run outside the store, the soldiers' positions every 8 s): the deck trooper west of the bait walked into the hatch at 5580 (5510-5650, between it and the player), fell through to the cap and into the sea; the road trooper stood at the road's hatch pressing down. The soldiers don't use the mod's ladders, and a walker falls into a 140 px hole. The hatches were widened (cycle 6) so a climber's body wouldn't snag their edges — since then a climber collides with nothing, so the hole only needs to show the way: 30 px, which walkers cross in their stride (the pontoon's hatch). The narrowed level lints clean (all objectives reachable, 62 ladder links).

frame-cost: perf with the player held at every spot (0 deaths, on foot, within the spot before and after): baseline 133; start 517 (320 draws), tower span 633 (688), deck 617 (621), road 383 (263): 4.76x. 34-46 soldiers asleep at each spot, 35-45 characters hidden off camera for the render. The cost is where the awake soldiers are.

Next: the mod with 30 px hatches (every shaft: the legs, the tower, the cliff, the bunker), baked; the play probe judging the respawn's place at the first moment back (and the descent loop ending once off the ladder at the foot; the bunker eye shot off the basement hatch); the in-loop frame matrix staged, to run the cycle after.
unknown: Why the flame heavy walks east each run (1017-1475 px), away from the bait.

respawn-works holds: first alive at x 13432 (8 px from the checkpoint at 13440), back on the catwalk at feet -330 within 5.2 s, still standing there 3 s on (x 13370). The move off the door fixed the point-blank respawn.

The narrow hatches changed the AI's paths as predicted: the shotgun hunter at (4100, -671), west of the old 140 px hatch at 5580, walked 1924 px to (6023, -731), 1270 px closer to the bait; the deck trooper west of the hatch walked to the player (5495 -> 5699, ending 105 px from the bait) instead of falling through. Ladders, co-op ladders, the tank and the boat still pass with them.

The probe's rule 'more than 150 px closer' misreads the residue ('the hunters walk towards a player ... at least three enemies move more than 150 px'): a hunter that starts 216 px away and walks up to the player (moved 207 px, ended 105 px off) can only be 110 px closer. The rule should count a hunter that closed 150 px OR came to the player (moved more than 150 px and ended within 200 px of it); falls, blasts and boat crews stay excluded. This refinement is being made after seeing cycle 14's data, under which it would give 3 (reached: the deck trooper; closed: the marksman 185, the shotgun hunter 1270) — so it is not credited from that data: it counts only if the re-run in the next cycle, with the new probe, shows it.

frame-cost: baseline 133; start 217, tower span 517, deck 750 (665 draws), road 417, the player held at every spot: 5.64x. The start spot fell from 517 to 217 between cycles (fewer awake soldiers near the dock this run), the deck rose from 617 to 750: the spots' cost moves with the fight, run to run.

Next: install the pathing probe with the refined rule (each hunter's reason recorded: closed / reached); run the in-loop frame matrix at the deck (baseline session, then the player held at (8300, -620), camera (8400, -700), three windows per step).

enemies-path holds on this cycle's run (not credited from cycle 14): movedCount 5 — the deck trooper reached the player (moved 174, ended beside it), the flame heavy closed 323, the marksman 440, the road trooper 219, the shotgun hunter from 4100 closed 517 — over 20.1 game seconds, player held (no deaths, on foot).

frame-cost, located: with the player held at (8300, -620): asIs 467 ms / 604 draws; every character drawn 433 (the off-camera hiding is within noise at this spot); wake window 1100 x 640 217 / 283 draws; all asleep 217; no enemies 150 / 211; no enemies + bridges hidden 117; + consoles 133, beacons 133, lights 150, ladders 150, towers 150; all sets hidden 117; half resolution 133. So: awake off-screen soldiers ~250 ms, asleep soldiers ~67 ms, the bridge set piece ~33 ms, the rest of the level at the baseline.
Four of the five hunters that came to the bait start inside a view-sized window (1100 x 640 about it): the pathing property survives cutting the wake window to the view.

Next: the mod with the wake window cut to the view (FAR 1100 x 640) and hooks to hide the bridge set piece's dressing and its hills apart; baked; the matrix extended (the wider window as a step, dressing and hills as kinds) and run; perf and every other probe re-run by the loop.
unknown: How many runs the pathing count needs to be judged fairly (it has read 1, 2, 2, 5, 0).

Correction: cycle 15's 'viewWake 217 ms' was confounded by step order — the matrix measures steps one after another at the same spot, and by that step the fight about the held player had died down (allAsleep, measured after it, read the same 217). This cycle, with the view-sized window installed, asIs read 417 and wideWake 433; the baseline itself read 183 against 133 before. The wake window is not the lever; the frame follows the live fight at the spot.

What holds across both matrix runs: with no enemies the deck is 150 ms (0.82-1.13x of each run's baseline); the set pieces together are ~33 ms (the bridge dressing, not the hills); half resolution changes little; no shader links. With the fight on, the deck reads 2.3-3.5x the baseline within a run, and perf's four spots 4.6-6.1x across cycles.

enemies-path: player held 20.3 game seconds (no deaths, 2 put-backs); movedCount 0 — the hunters in the window were awake and moved (the deck trooper 697, the heavy 475, the road trooper 1553) but away from the bait; the shotgun hunter from 4100, outside the view-sized window, never woke. Cycle 15, same level but for the window, gave 5. The count swings with the AI's choices from run to run.

Put the wake window back to 1700 x 800 (it bought nothing measurable and cost the far hunters), bake, and let the loop re-observe. If frame-cost stays above 1.5x, which every measurement with the fight on says it will, the threshold under the software renderer is the human's decision.

DISCRIMINATING_EXPERIMENT: Two residues are now governed by run-to-run variance, not by a defect the next edit can remove. enemies-path has read 1, 2, 2, 5, 0 across cycles with the level essentially unchanged: a single 20-game-second trial samples the AI's choice once. frame-cost reads 2.3-3.5x (matrix, deck) and 4.6-6.1x (perf, worst of four spots) with the fight on, and 0.8-1.1x with no enemies; the one lever tried last cycle (a view-sized wake window) showed no saving that held, and cost the far hunters. Repeating edits against single noisy runs is the failed approach.
unknown: The same measurement on a hardware GPU.
enemies-path holds as a property of the level, not of one run: trial counts 3, 3, 4 with the flame heavy closing 345-422 px in all three and the deck troopers closing or reaching the player.

frame-cost remains 3.76x at the fight spots (tower span, deck 500 ms) while the spots without a fight (start, road 217 ms) are 1.6x. Across cycles 11-17 the worst spot read 3.7-6.1x; with no enemies the deck reads 0.8-1.1x of its run's baseline; the set pieces together are ~33 ms; neither the wake window nor off-camera culling moved the fight's cost reliably.

The remaining gap is the engine drawing a live fight (awake soldiers firing at a god-mode player) under a software rasteriser, measured against a start map with no fight. Closing it inside the level means removing soldiers from the fight spots — against the intent's own dense foundation fights. Whether the 1.5x threshold applies to that measurement is the human's call; the loop does not move the threshold.
